_comment: Rule-tag census for tools/check-rule-tags.py. A root absent on a box makes the census exit 2 for that run, never a zero count. A rule is enforced ([enforced: <path relative to root>] inline, or a rule_map sidecar entry), judgement or record (both excluded from the coverage denominator) or prose; an enforcer must be WIRED in: a non-comment line of an invocation_surfaces file resolves to it (list a test file as a surface only if a hook or CI job runs it), and each enforced rule carries an anchor found in the enforcer. floor_schedule is the rising ratchet that --check enforces. root_candidates: tried in order, then root; a relative one resolves against this bus clone. DIAGNOSTIC in --report mode; a project may wire --check as its own gate. The DNG bullet regex matches the 138 units R-D2 reports (117 in docs/14 + 21 in AGENTS.md, whole files, no section) because DNG rules are bold-led paragraphs and numbered items as well as dash bullets.

projects.name: cloudvore
projects._comment: Cloudvore's operating contract and its children (K155, landed at Cloudvore c305770, 2026-10-18). A rule is a '-' or numbered item or a '**'-led paragraph; a '*' item is context, not a rule. Cloudvore's own gate is tools/rule-tags.py (tools bar REQUIRED), which also refuses a lost, demoted or un-enforced rule against the base commit; this census is the fleet's read of the same grammar. The main checkout can lag origin/master: measure with --root at a checkout of origin/master. No invocation_surfaces and no floor yet: Cloudvore credits wiring at runtime (tools/run-tools-bar.py required_names(), which names suites without the tools/ prefix), which this census's text match cannot see, so the 16 backed rules are existence-checked here only; a Cloudvore row teaches the census that wiring before a floor is set.
